one_month_reasoning: In-window events: (1) Q3 2026 results expected ~Oct 22 (unconfirmed; some calendars show Oct 15). Q3 guidance was 750 Mlb copper sales at $2.00/lb unit cost with H2 price assumption $6.00/lb; LME copper averaged well above that in Q3 (record $14,875/t on Sep 10, ~$6.56/lb at Sep 30) and COMEX carries a tariff premium, so realized price should beat the deck (~$150M OCF per $0.10/lb for H2), making a modest beat likely; the bigger swing factor is the Grasberg ramp commentary (65% H2-26, 80% mid-27) and any first 2027 volume outlook. (2) White House decision on the Commerce-recommended 15% refined-copper tariff from Jan 2027 is still pending after the Sep 29 checkpoint; a tariff would widen the COMEX premium (mildly positive for FCX's US cathode sales) but could hit LME sentiment. (3) Supply-side news: Cobre Panama restart recommendation reached the Panamanian president Sep 30 (mildly bearish copper at the margin, but tonnage only matters from 2027+), Centinela strike vote (bullish), China PMI back above 50. Net: slight positive tilt from likely price-driven beat, centred ~$71 with monthly vol ~13.5% (48%/3.5), i.e. close to symmetric.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward EV/EBITDA (8.5x 2028E EBITDA of ~$16.5B at $5.75/lb copper, less ~30% NCI and ~$4B net debt incl. smelter debt = ~$65) and forward P/E (18x 2028E EPS ~$3.90 = ~$70), valuing the stock as the market will at Sep-2027 when it looks through to a fully restored Grasberg.

bear.story: Copper retreats to ~$4.75/lb as tariff-driven stock build unwinds, Cobre Panama restarts and China demand softens; Grasberg ramp slips (PB1 delay, another incident) or Indonesian export/smelter friction; multiple compresses to ~7x.

base.story: Copper holds $5.50-6.25 on concentrate deficit (zero/negative TC/RCs, ICSG deficits 2026-27); Grasberg reaches ~80% mid-27 and market values FCX on 2028 full-run EBITDA ~$16B at 8.5x.

bull.story: Structural deficit deepens (Chile strikes, grade decline, AI/grid demand), copper $7+/lb, US refined tariff lifts COMEX premium for FCX's US cathode; Grasberg at full rate early; EBITDA $20B+ at 9x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$48 (-32%) the market would be pricing copper near $4.75/lb or a failed Grasberg restoration; with LME near records and concentrate markets in historic deficit, that level most likely signals a fundamental break (Grasberg setback, Indonesian policy action on PTFI, or a demand shock), not noise.

reasoning: Industry lane: the value chain says mine supply is the binding constraint — 2026 TC/RC benchmark settled at zero and spot TC/RCs went negative (-$127/t in June), ICSG projects refined deficits in 2026 and tightening into 2027, peers (Southern Copper, Antofagasta) are flat-to-down in H1 output, Centinela faces a strike vote, and Cobre Panama only adds ~70kt of stockpile until a restart decision. That supports copper staying elevated (LME ~$14,400/t, ~$6.5/lb) though Goldman and others expect some mean reversion from records, and part of the COMEX strength is tariff speculation (SocGen: premium implies ~15% odds of Jan-27 tariff). For FCX specifically, the Grasberg ramp (65%->80%->~full by end-27) lifts copper sales from 3.1bn lb in 2026 toward ~4.1bn lb, so by Sep-2027 investors will price 2028 full-run earnings. At a haircut $5.75 deck my EV/EBITDA and P/E both land $65-70, i.e. the stock at $70.58 already discounts recovery plus a high copper price; upside needs copper to stay above $6. With no valuation edge I centre the 12-month distribution slightly above spot (~$71.5 median, ~dividend/drift) with ~44% lognormal vol (below the 48% realized which included the Grasberg shock) and slightly fatter left tail for a commodity miner.
